classification.difficultyReason: Requires finding a common ringing time for four fractional intervals by converting to a common time unit and applying prime factorisation.

content.prompt: Four different bells ring every $\frac{5}{4}$ seconds, $\frac{6}{5}$ seconds, $\frac{7}{6}$ seconds and $\frac{8}{7}$ seconds. If all four bells ring at the same time, then how long is it before they next ring at the same time?

answer.short:
$840$ seconds.

Express the intervals in a common time unit and find their LCM.
answer.worked:
Use $\frac{1}{420}$ second as the time unit, since $\operatorname{LCM}(4,5,6,7)=420$. The four intervals are then $525$, $504$, $490$ and $480$ units.

$$\begin{align*}525&=3\times5^2\times7\\504&=2^3\times3^2\times7\\490&=2\times5\times7^2\\480&=2^5\times3\times5\end{align*}$$

Take the greatest power of each prime:

$$\begin{align*}\operatorname{LCM}(525,504,490,480)&=2^5\times3^2\times5^2\times7^2\\\operatorname{LCM}(525,504,490,480)&=352800.\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\text{Time}&=\frac{352800}{420}\text{ seconds}\\\text{Time}&=840\text{ seconds}.\end{align*}$$
